subject.title: message tool should auto-select the only enabled account

question: Should omitted message-tool account IDs infer a single enabled configured account after explicit/default/bound precedence, or should OpenClaw keep requiring explicit `accountId` or `defaultAccount` when the configured default is disabled?
rationale: The implementation boundary is clear, but this changes compatibility-sensitive fallback behavior for existing multi-account configurations and the linked implementation PR is not landable yet.

options.title: Accept Shared Resolver Policy
options.body: Land or replace the linked PR with a shared resolver that picks an enabled configured default account or exactly one enabled configured account, with clear zero-or-multiple errors.

options.title: Keep Explicit Account Selection
options.body: Keep current semantics and document that users must pass `accountId` or configure `defaultAccount` when the configured default is disabled.

options.title: Require Channel-Owned Fallback
options.body: Ask for channel-specific behavior if maintainers do not want core to own omitted-account fallback policy across message channels.

recommendation.title: Accept Shared Resolver Policy
recommendation.body: Land or replace the linked PR with a shared resolver that picks an enabled configured default account or exactly one enabled configured account, with clear zero-or-multiple errors.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete already supplied the prior shared-resolver direction and has the strongest history signal across account-helper and outbound routing policy.
